findings.impact: Output construction and hashing scale approximately with goal-count times binding-size. With up to 4096 prepared obligations, legal bounded input can cause multi-gigabyte transient object/string allocation, consume the 12-GiB process-tree budget or 30-second phase budget, and make a request incomplete before the intended output fallback is reached. The supervisor preserves the hard ceiling and no authority is promoted, but this is substantial avoidable resource amplification on accepted input.
findings.recommendation: Keep the owned binding once at plan level and attach a canonical binding digest/reference to each goal (with the plan identity committing both), or preflight the expanded representation with a bounded counter and reject before deep copies/serialization.
findings.title: Avoid quadratic checkpoint-binding duplication before the output bound
findings.trigger: A valid near-8-MiB correspondence with many original premise occurrences. The binding includes the full interpretation/object map and an ordered copy of every premise/provider observation; `build_context_goals` deep-copies that binding into every generated obligation and hashes each expanded row. The worker then calls `json.dumps` on the entire expanded result before checking whether it exceeds 8 MiB.

limitations: This is source-first audit only. Root owns real native plan/check replay, broader task 1.2 integration, and final gates. The scoped capability remains distinct from the norm-route bridge and does not close task 1.2.

reviewed.checkpoint: Checking regenerates the complete plan and requires exact planId equality before term dispatch; unknown goal IDs reject. Accepted support requires replay/trust acceptance for every generated goal and no residuals.
reviewed.dispatch: Both new commands are parsed and dispatched through proof_contract_cli; terms and request files share an 8 MiB raw input cap.
reviewed.freshSource: Stored source digest, fresh scoped extraction sliceId, parent declaration observation/environment, strict prefix digest, and end-of-stage source reread are bound. The generated prefix is compiled with checks that the parent declaration and original module are absent.
reviewed.nativeOwnership: Validated native envelope batch; correspondence owner and exact interpretation owner are resolved by typed artifact ref and subject. The correspondence payload is regenerated from the native interpretation, stored actual slice, and object map; every semantic payload field except the normalized correspondenceId is compared. Interpretation/source-map association and exact source anchor are revalidated against repoRoot.
reviewed.obligations: Prepared obligations must all be open and duplicate IDs/domain injection are rejected. Original row order is preserved; premise/provider occurrence IDs are reattached from the actual selected slice. Domain membership witnesses are separate from representation typing and semantic conclusion. Residuals prevent checked-support.
reviewed.resourceStops: Preparation is supervised as one process-tree stage with bridge limits capped at 30 seconds, 12 GiB RSS and 8 MiB output under the supplied absolute deadline; per-goal check stages are supervised under the same deadline. Resource stop aliases are recursively recognized, and there is no retry path.
reviewed.tests: No tests or Lean/source workflows were run in this audit. Frozen boundary/checkpoint test file hashes were verified unchanged. Targeted Ruff check passed.
